solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pass on characteristic feature when bearing new son, Mike

indicators.note: a thing bearing something carries it within, so the trait holds the three letters

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic feature
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone passes on a family trait now that a baby boy called Mike has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when bearing' makes TRAIT carry N, S and M in its middle: TRA-NSM-IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit something is a synonym for passing it on, as with a message or a gene.

clue.text: Caught short in flipping Tesco, Morecambe, needing privy

indicators.note: flipping, as a mild oath or as tossing over, tells us to jumble the letters left
caught short here means the word for caught is cut out, left short of it

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Eric Morecambe was half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: Comedian Eric Morecambe is caught short in a Tesco supermarket and urgently needs a toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes C from TESCO, leaving TESO; 'flipping' rearranges that into ESOT. 'Privy' looks like a lavatory, which fits the caught-short story, but here it is the adjective meaning secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Privy as an adjective means known only to a select few, which is what esoteric knowledge is.

clue.text: Actor that works hard with family filling skips by house (US city)

indicators.note: by means next to, so these letters stand beside the next part

parts.note: the ant is the proverbial hard worker
NY is New York

indicators.note: the word for family fills the word for skips

parts.note: skips means hops
kin means family

explanation.surface: An actor and his relatives pack the rubbish skips beside a house in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Skips here are leaps, not British rubbish containers. The answer is the Welsh actor Sir Anthony Hopkins.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Anthony Hopkins is a famous Welsh film and stage actor, an example of the category.

clue.text: It may result from punch mum accepted and drained earlier

parts.note: mum as in keep mum: SH is the call for silence
in means accepted, as in fashionable or admitted

indicators.note: drained means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outside letters of the word earlier

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a mother who took a punch after earlier drinking the glass dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but is the instruction to be quiet. 'Punch' tempts as the drink beside 'drained'; it is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A black eye is commonly called a shiner, the bruise a punch to the face leaves.

clue.text: Number 10 defends British railway system that develops after congress

indicators.note: to defend is to surround protectively, so the music word wraps the other letters

parts.note: this points to the answer of the clue numbered 10, a style of music

explanation.surface: Downing Street defends the British railway network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 10' suggests Downing Street, the British Prime Minister's residence; it is the answer to 10 across. 'Congress' means sexual intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is the organism that grows after conception, which follows sexual intercourse, here coyly called congress.

clue.text: Perennial track, 'Southern Hymn', embraced by friend

indicators.note: the friend word hugs the run of letters formed by the next three pieces

parts.note: chum means friend
RY, railway, is a track
an anthem is a hymn

explanation.surface: A friend embraces a southern hymn as a music track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' reads as a song but gives the railway abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The chrysanthemum is a garden flower that comes back year after year, a perennial plant.

clue.text: Dave's partner, having much time at home, is inclined to pursue illusory hopes

parts.note: Chas and Dave were a London pub-rock singing duo
an era is a long period of time
in means at home
bows means bends or inclines

explanation.surface: Dave's partner, retired and home a lot, is given to chasing dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAS of the British duo Chas and Dave, known for cockney sing-along songs.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase rainbows is an idiom for pursuing unrealistic goals that can never be reached.

clue.text: Pacific Islands informed creative person. Dan perhaps

indicators.note: informed in the sense of told or spoken, so the island name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: the Marshall Islands lie in the Pacific
an artist is a creative person

explanation.surface: Someone from the Pacific islands tells an artist something; perhaps that someone is called Dan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dan' looks like a man's name, but a dan is a black-belt grade in judo or karate.
explanation.definitionFit: A dan is a grade held in judo or karate, so its holder is an example of a fighter in those sports.

clue.text: Go from north-east to take home bird

parts.note: gan is the Geordie dialect word for go, used in north-east England
to net is to take home as pay after deductions

explanation.surface: A traveller sets off from north-east England to take a bird home.
explanation.definitionFit: The gannet is a large seabird, an example of the category; it nests on north-east coasts too.

clue.text: Nominal antique's stored indoors periodically

indicators.note: the old word has the picked letters stored inside it

parts.note: hoary means very old, antique; the 's is has

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so take every other letter of indoors

explanation.surface: A notional antique is kept indoors from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nominal' is the definition, in its sense of in name only, not the small-amount sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorary title is nominal: it carries the name without the duties or pay.

clue.text: Revolutionary 'ouse music?

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a cockney dropping the h of house; the word home, said the same way, loses its h too

explanation.surface: Cockney house music is described as revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe shows an h dropped: house becomes home, which loses its H to leave OME, read backwards. 'Ouse' also pretends to be the house music style.
explanation.definitionFit: Emo is a style of emotional rock music; the question mark flags that it is an example.

clue.text: Advise American to catch cricket fixture?

indicators.note: the phrase is told to catch, that is contain, the answer inside its letters

explanation.surface: Someone tells an American how to catch a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'adviSE AMERican'. 'Cricket fixture' looks like a match, but means a regular in the side, the question mark warning of the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamer is a seam bowler, a fast bowler who may be a permanent member, a fixture, of a cricket team.

clue.text: Numbing area up north inhabited by nothing after November

indicators.note: after means the rest of the letters follow the N

parts.note: November is N in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: the area is inhabited by, so contains, the nothing letter

parts.note: the Arctic is the region around the North Pole
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A northern region left empty after November has a numbing chill.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic drug dulls the senses, so the adjective describes something numbing.

clue.text: Classical symbol that starts a book?

definitions.meaning: a letter of the Greek alphabet
Ch 1, chapter one, is where a book starts

explanation.surface: An ancient emblem appears on a book's opening page.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as CH I: chapter one.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is the twenty-second letter of the Greek alphabet, a symbol from the classical world.

clue.text: 'Standard' has jerk finally back on list for transfer disrupting the football club

indicators.note: has joins the pieces in order

parts.note: par is a standard or norm
a tic is an involuntary jerk

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of back
disrupting means breaking into, so the scrambled letters split the word
a player on the list for transfer is moving, so these letters move about

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports that the football club's jerk is back on the transfer list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for transfer' shuffles LIST into ISTL, which 'disrupting' puts inside THE. Partick Thistle is a Scottish football club in Glasgow. 'Standard' tempts as the newspaper's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Partick Thistle is a professional football club based in Glasgow, an example of the category.

clue.text: That man's height is taken down loosely

indicators.note: in a down clue taken down means moved to the bottom

parts.note: his means belonging to that man

explanation.surface: A man's height is measured somewhat loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix or word ish means approximately, used to say something is roughly so.

clue.text: See 14
Part of diamond maybe with hole getting repaired in socks

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the socks word

parts.note: hose means socks or stockings

indicators.note: being repaired means put back together in a new order
with a hole in it, the word loses its middle letter

explanation.surface: Holed socks are being darned, perhaps with part of a diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with hole' cuts the middle out of 'maybe' to leave MABE, which 'getting repaired' shuffles. The diamond is a baseball field, not a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: Home base is the plate on a baseball diamond, one of the four bases at its corners.

clue.text: Betting club date produced a long streak?

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds offered at the off
a lodge is a club, such as a Masonic one

explanation.surface: A betting club's date produced a long winning run.
explanation.walkthrough: A streak tempts as a winning run of bets; here it is a smear.
explanation.definitionFit: To splodge is to make a blot or smear, which a long streak of paint or ink would be.

clue.text: See 3
Villain perhaps knocked about in hands of a Roman emperor

indicators.note: being in the hands of means held inside the a and emperor letters

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for knocked is read backwards

parts.note: hit means knocked

explanation.surface: A villain is roughed up by a Roman emperor's men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the knock word round; 'in hands of' has the A and the emperor hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain who is the main character of a story can be a protagonist lacking heroic qualities.

clue.text: Running short distance with pointer heartless

parts.note: IN is the abbreviation for inch, a short distance

indicators.note: heartless means with the middle letter cut out

parts.note: an arrow is a pointer

explanation.surface: Running a short way with a dog that has no heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointer' suggests the gun dog; it is an arrow sign. 'heartless' removes its middle R.
explanation.definitionFit: Running means consecutively, as in three wins running, one after another without break.

clue.text: Through summer in Provence, coach card game

indicators.note: the coach goes through, inside, the French word

parts.note: été is French for summer
a car is a railway coach

explanation.surface: A coach goes through Provence in summer for a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach suggests a bus; it is a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Écarté is a nineteenth-century card game for two players, an example of the category.

clue.text: Aristocratic address centres on family plot and garden

indicators.note: the centres of these three words supply the letters, two from each

explanation.surface: A noble's address concentrates on his family plot and garden.
explanation.definitionFit: My lord was the old form of address used when speaking to a nobleman.

clue.text: Europe's borders set down on page in letter

indicators.note: the edge letters are written after the page letter
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Europe's frontiers are drawn on a page in a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pee is the name of the alphabet letter P when spelt out.

clue.text: Weapon plant not needing to sell

indicators.note: not needing means the following word is dropped

parts.note: the tomato is a plant
to hawk is to sell goods by calling out

explanation.surface: A plant that needs no selling.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the final TO from TOMATO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomahawk is a light axe used by Native Americans as a tool and weapon.

clue.text: Newsmen probe minute accommodation

indicators.note: to probe is to go into, so the newsmen go inside

parts.note: a bit means a tiny amount, a minute amount
eds are editors, senior newsmen

explanation.surface: Journalists investigate tiny lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' reads as the noun, sixty seconds; it is the adjective tiny. A bedsit is a British one-room rented flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single rented room used for living and sleeping, a kind of housing.

clue.text: During film, Dr Watson appears terribly abrupt

indicators.note: during means within, so the shuffled letters go inside

parts.note: a sheet is a thin film of material

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the doctor's name is jumbled

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes's partner turns up curtly in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' jumbles the doctor's name, which 'During' sets inside the film word. 'Film' looks like a movie but is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Short and sweet is an idiom for brief and to the point, which can come across as curt.
